messages:
eli: Heads-up — seeing a regression on L4/T4 inference runs when KV cache is warm. seqlen ~384, steady-state p95 jumped from ~88ms to ~210ms after yesterday's runtime change. Anyone seen similar?

matt: ugh. can you paste the profiling snapshot? is it kernel selection flipping to a slower path?

eli: Perf snapshot: p95 88ms -> 210ms, p50 42ms -> 60ms. CPU churn low, GPU util OK. Looks like more time in attention kernel and memcpy spikes. Perf-bot uploaded trace: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/1719994500 (public link for engineers) :eyes:

perf-bot: uploaded flamegraph + timeline for 1719994500 -> https://perf.redwood/internal/artifacts/1719994500/flame.html

jia: quick skim — kernel selector seems to pick the 'wide-tile' attention kernel for seqlen 384 on L4/T4 after last autotune change. That kernel is memory-bound on smaller GPUs; on A100/H100 it wins. Cross-device delta.

anuj: yep, we tuned autotuner to favor throughput for A100/H100 and didn't put a hard device-family penalty. L4/T4 have lower mem BW and different L2 caching behavior. With KV warm and continuous batching the selector should prefer the smaller-tile kernel on those devices.

sofia: can we add a seqlen-aware device-family rule? e.g. if device in {L4,T4,A10} && seqlen in [256,512] favor kernel C (small-tile, lower mem-bandwidth)

matt: agree. Also consider KV-cache hit ratio — when hit_ratio > 0.8 we should bias toward kernels with cheaper KV access. Right now selector only looks at flops / latency model.

eli: here's the relevant snippet from the selector (post-change):
```
// simplified
if (predict_throughput(kernelB, metadata) > predict_throughput(kernelA))
   pick kernelB;
else
   pick kernelA;
```
We need device-bandwidth and kv-hit into predict_throughput.

jia: i'll run a microbenchmark matrix across devices (L4/T4/A10/A100/H100) for seqlens [64,128,256,384,512] and batch sizes [1,2,4,8]. Will capture kernel timings + memcpy.

matt: nice. add quantized (4-bit) path too if you can. Past regressions hit the quant path unexpectedly.

anuj: for immediate mitigation can we add a temporary preset 'device-family-fallback-smalltile' that forces small-tile kernels for L4/T4/A10 for seqlen >= 256? Then we can flip it in prod while autotuner learns.

eli: please do that as a canary on our dedicated pool. Add rollout = 10% and automatic rollback on error/latency breach.

sofia: i'll draft the preset config in console (JSON) and link it. something like:
```
{
  "name": "canary-smalltile-seqlen-256-512",
  "devices": ["L4","T4","A10"],
  "seqlen_range": [256,512],
  "kernel_preference": ["small_tile_attn", "fallback"],
  "rollout": 0.1
}
```

matt: also add a perf regression alert: p95 > baseline * 1.4 for that pool. We can tie to token-level dashboards.

eli: thanks. is anyone worried about cost regressions on A100/H100 from that preset? We need it scoped to device family only.

jia: will scope it. My benchmark will produce a decision matrix; i’ll attach CSV + flamegraphs. Expect uploads in ~2 hours.

perf-bot: benchmark job queued (id=bnch-1719994500). status: running.

anuj: postmortem note: root cause likely autotuner's recent global scoring tweak that removed an explicit device-family penalty. Fix plan: (1) apply canary preset; (2) enrich throughput predictor with device_mem_bw and kv_hit_ratio; (3) retrain autotuner scoring on cross-device microbench corpus; (4) add seqlen-device heuristic as fallback.

eli: perfect. assign owners: matt - canary preset + rollout; jia - microbench + artifacts; anuj - scoring change; sofia - alert + console config; i'll monitor and coordinate. :thumbsup:

matt: created canary config, starting rollout to 10% on Dedicated L4 pool. link: https://console.redwood/presets/1719994500

jia: uploaded preliminary CSV + flamegraphs: https://perf.redwood/internal/artifacts/1719994500/bench.csv and /flame.zip. early signal: L4 small_tile wins for seqlen>=256 (p95 down ~35%), A100 prefers wide-tile.

eli: great. leaving this thread open until canary stabilizes. thanks folks.

sofia: copying note to eng-runtime runbook and incident tracker.

perf-bot: canary metrics (10m window): p95 for canary pods = 92ms (baseline 210ms) on L4 pool. auto-rollback not triggered. :white_check_mark:
